title: LA28 opens new commercial avenue as Allianz secures beach arena naming rights
article_text:
Allianz has expanded its Olympic and Paralympic Games partnership by securing naming rights to the Allianz Beach Arena, a temporary venue in Long Beach, California, that will host beach volleyball at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games and blind football during the Paralympic Games. The agreement brings the insurer’s global sporting partnerships together at a single competition venue.

The arena is scheduled to host 39 Olympic beach volleyball matches, including two medal events, and 10 Paralympic blind football matches, including one medal event. The German insurer estimates that the venue will accommodate nearly 15,000 spectators per session and attract approximately 735,000 spectators across both competitions, providing the brand with visibility across two major international sporting events.

The agreement makes the Allianz Beach Arena the eighth venue in the company’s Family of Stadiums, which includes Allianz Arena in Munich, Allianz Stadium in Sydney and Allianz Field in Minnesota. More significantly, it represents the first time an Olympic competition venue will carry a commercial partner’s name, according to the International Olympic Committee (IOC). The arrangement reflects LA28’s efforts to develop new commercial opportunities through venue naming rights.

Eike Bürgel, Global Head of Olympic and Paralympic Program at Allianz, said, “For the first time, two of Allianz’s major sports initiatives – the Allianz Family of Stadiums and our Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic partnership – come together in one venue that proudly bears the Allianz name. Beach Volleyball broke attendance records at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, and having the Allianz name on its arena at the LA28 Games is a unique way to bring our brand closer to fans and strengthen our visibility as a Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic Partner.”

The insurance group is a Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic Partner, with its agreement extending through the Brisbane 2032 Games. The company has also introduced a customised version of the LA28 emblem inspired by Allianz Arena and Allianz Field, linking its existing stadium portfolio with its Olympic and Paralympic involvement.

The deal establishes a new commercial platform for the financial services group while illustrating how LA28 is creating additional sponsorship opportunities around its competition venues.

title: Capital.com Australian Open Elevates Ares and Renews AWS and Fortinet Partnerships for 2026 Tournament
article_text:
The Capital.com Australian Open has announced a series of commercial sponsorship agreements ahead of its 2026 event, elevating alternative investment manager Ares Management to Major Partner status and securing one-year partnership renewals with technology leaders Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Fortinet.

The commercial deals strengthen the tournament’s tier-one sponsor portfolio as momentum builds for the 2026 championship, scheduled for December 3–6 at Kingston Heath Golf Club in Melbourne.

The event—co-sanctioned by the Challenger PGA Tour of Australasia and DP World Tour—will feature a marquee international field headlined by back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy.

Highlighting how integration with global tech brands enhances both fan and tournament infrastructure, chief commercial officer at Golf Australia and the PGA of Australia, Ben Sellenger, said: “The calibre and number of businesses that want to be part of the Capital.com Australian Open continues to grow, and these three partnerships are a great example of that.”

“We are delighted to welcome back Ares, AWS and Fortinet.

“All are global leaders in their respective fields and have a significant presence in international sports, including golf.

“With AWS helping us deliver our inaugural tournament app and Fortinet bringing its global cybersecurity expertise to the championship, these partnerships also demonstrate how our commercial partners can play a genuine role in enhancing the tournament experience.

“The Capital.com Australian Open is becoming an increasingly attractive platform for global brands, and we are proud to have Ares, AWS and Fortinet continuing to sponsor the championship,” Sellenger said.

title: Sprite’s NBA comeback: How Coca-Cola is reimagining a storied sponsorship for basketball’s new era
article_text:
There are some sponsorship deals that arrive at just the right time.

Sprite was the official soft drink of the National Basketball Association (NBA) from 1994 to 2015.

It had been involved with the league since 1986, but this bigger partnership launched as Sprite began setting out a new brand identity. Early in the sports drink boom and with another skirmish unfolding in the cola wars, it drew on Gen X irony and irreverence to give consumers a simpler call to action.

Its ‘obey your thirst’ pitch – the digested message of which was ‘ignore the noise, this lemon-lime drink is refreshing’ – used knowing and zeitgeisty humour to carve a slice of the counterculture for a brand owned by Coca-Cola.

The energy it generated was a good match for the NBA: youthful and dynamic, cutting through some of the earnestness and bombast that characterised sports marketing elsewhere. Between smart creative and a sharp sense of the basketball universe beyond the big league, Sprite left a lasting impression.

It never quite left the court – as of last season, it still had deals with 17 individual NBA teams. But in March, after 11 years away, The Coca-Cola Company confirmed a multi-season global partnership to restore Sprite to its former league-wide category, replacing PepsiCo’s Mountain Dew and Starry drinks.

“I’m super proud and excited that Sprite is back,” says Mickael Vinet, vice president of global sports, music, entertainment partnerships and marketing for Coca-Cola. “And not only would I say it’s back in basketball globally, but I truly believe it is here to stay.”

For Vinet, this is a particularly meaningful reunion. The Frenchman has spent 26 years at Coca-Cola, having started as an intern in the sports and entertainment team in his homeland. Sprite’s NBA work was prominent in his early career; its comeback was “one of the first partnership opportunities” that arose after he assumed his current role in 2025.

This revival, he says, “has created “a lot of excitement” at the prospect of “connecting fans across sport, music, fashion, and the culture around it”.

For all that, the new partnership is dropping into a very different brand and media environment. The ‘Never Stop Refreshing The Game’ concept, launched just before the tip-off of the 2026/27 season, must exist in a context where the brand no longer has “one claim and one advertisement” under its command.

In restoring Sprite’s connection with the NBA today, Vinet and his team must “bring the campaign to life” on multiple platforms across 25 fast-moving markets.

The NBA sponsorship restates a specific role for Sprite within the Coca-Cola suite of products.

“On Brand Coke,” Vinet says, “we are very connected with the Olympic movement, with football. And I think Sprite and basketball should be what Coke is around football. I think that’s a simple way to visualise the ambition.”

Vinet believes Sprite retains a natural fit with the “values” and “culture” of the basketball audience. The execution of this new campaign, however, will depend on finding “the right insight” to build a productive commercial relationship.

Beyond its associations with individual teams, Sprite’s presence in the NBA has already been refreshed through an endorsement deal with Minnesota Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards. In 2024, he fronted the restoration of the ‘Obey Your Thirst’ tagline.

One early commercial appearance sees Edwards complete a dunk in front of an awed fan, who then notices the serial All-Star take a swig from a bottle of Sprite. The fan enjoys the same drink but his attempt to complete a dunk of his own ends in disaster. The ad is a winking retread of a mid-90s effort featuring Grant Hill, which made a similarly low promises about the powers of the central product.

Hill himself contributes the voiceover: “You want to hoop like Anthony Edwards? Practice. You want a refreshing drink? Obey your thirst.”

Edwards has now been joined on the Sprite roster by Denver Nuggets icon Nikola Jokić. Released in October, the three-time league MVP’s introduction has a similar tone but hits fewer nostalgic notes. He appears on a comedy club stage, drinking Sprite and delivering spare, flat standup to a mostly quiet audience. As the spot ends, the text reads: ‘Jokes aside, welcome Joker.’

“I think what is interesting with the two is they have different perspectives, different personalities, different journeys,” Vinet says. “But they both have this unique edge that they will bring to what we do, and what will be very important is not just to have them as ambassadors, but to bring their stories and their views in the way we communicate and engage with fans.”

Jokić also serves as a reminder of how the NBA’s profile has changed in the past decade. He was one of 125 overseas players listed on opening week rosters for 2026/27. International recruitment was very much a feature of the NBA by the end of Sprite’s first run in 2015, but the achievements since then of stars like the 31-year-old Serbian has confirmed its status as a truly global competition.

To put it another way, Sprite will need a much more internationally focused strategy this time around. Between another annual run of regular season games outside North America – beginning in early November with the NBA Mexico City Game before stops in Paris and Manchester next January – and much-publicised long-term ambitions in Europe, the NBA offers a broader platform than ever before.

title: Mitsubishi Electric in Nordic Combined partnership with skiing’s FIS
article_text:
The International Ski & Snowboard Federation (FIS) governing body has continued its recent commercial push by bringing in electronics and electrical equipment manufacturer Mitsubishi Electric as a new sponsor.

The partnership will be centred around the Nordic Combined discipline and sees Mitsubishi Electric become the title partner of the FIS Nordic Combined World Cup.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

In addition, the brand will become a premium partner for the FIS Tour de Ski series for 2026-27.

The 2026-27 FIS Nordic Combined World Cup begins in late November in Ruka, Finland.

Earlier this week, the FIS announced an extension of its 20-year partnership with Swiss watchmaker Longines, which is set to continue as the official timekeeper for events in the Alpine skiing discipline.

June, meanwhile, saw the governing body extend its major tie-up with carmaker Audi – the title sponsor for the Alpine Ski World Cup, among other designations – through to 2030.

Mitsubishi Electric is also a commercial partner of the World Rugby governing body, covering the women's national team WXV Global Series, and of Premiership Women's Rugby in England.

title: Sportradar and Dortmund extend integrity agreement
article_text:
German soccer heavyweights Borussia Dortmund have extended their integrity services provision tie-up with Sportradar, the sports technology and data giant.

Through an exclusive agreement unveiled yesterday, Sportradar will continue to conduct background investigations into potential sponsors and partners of the West German club.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The subsequent reports will analyse corporate structures, the brand's ownership, its licensing agreements, key personnel, business operations, and levels of regulatory compliance.

In addition, Sportradar will establish whether there are any criminal or legal proceedings at play that could create a risk for Borussia Dortmund in terms of its own brand reputation.

Andreas Krannich, executive vice president for integrity services at Sportradar, commented: "Borussia Dortmund recognizes the importance of building partnerships that reflect the club’s values, resonate with its supporters and create sustainable value for all parties involved. We are delighted to continue supporting the club as it develops a strong ecosystem of trusted commercial relationships that contribute positively to its long-term ambitions.”

Sportradar also has an integrity services partnership in place with soccer's global governing body FIFA, extended earlier this year and running through 2031.

In terms of recent Borussia Dortmund commercial activity, meanwhile, this month has already seen the club announce a new deal with AI-powered tech firm Freedom2hear.

Freedom2hear is now utilizing its patented AI to filter “harmful content”, termed “hate speech, harassment, pornography, spam and illegal broadcast links”, from Dortmund’s social media channels, in order to safeguard fans.

In September, meanwhile, the club extended its deal with IT service provider Adesso for another four years to run through the Bundesliga 2029-30 campaign.

The Sportfive agency serves as the club's commercial partner agency of record through 2030-31.

Dortmund currently sit joint top of the 18-team Bundesliga, after seven matchdays of the 2026-27 season.

title: Legends in as operator for record-breaking new Hanoi stadium
article_text:
Legends Global, the venue management and premium experiences firm, has been brought in as the operating partner for a new, 135,000-capacity, sports stadium that will open in the Vietnam capital of Hanoi in 2027.

A deal has been unveiled today between Legends and Vingroup, the largest Vietnamese private conglomerate, through which Legends will play a heavy role in operating the new VinFast-Trong Dong Stadium, set to open at the end of July next year.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The tie-up entails Vingroup and Legends Global working collaboratively to oversee and manage the venue, and to attract major events – from the worlds of sport, culture, and entertainment – to the event. A planned capacity of 135,000 would make it the largest stadium to be used for sport worldwide.

Legends will be involved in facility management, vendor coordination, as well as on-site service operations.

The two parties have said the arena will "establish new benchmarks in scale and technological sophistication."

It will also work to develop the venue management staff working for Vingroup in Vietnam.

In addition, the overall partnership between the two parties will stretch into Legends providing wider stadium and event management services to Vingroup in the country.

Dan Levy, chief executive at Legends Global, commented: "Legends Global is honoured to partner with Vingroup on this landmark development. We look forward to sharing our expertise in venue and event management to help bring Vingroup’s ambition and vision for the world’s largest stadium to life.”

Nguyen Viet Quang, Vingroup's vice chair and CEO, added: "With its world-leading scale, contemporary architecture inspired by Vietnamese cultural heritage, automated retractable roof, and playing surface designed to meet FIFA standards, we envision working alongside Legends Global to transform the stadium into a global gathering place for the finest sporting, cultural, and entertainment events.”

The plan is currently for the VinFast-Trong Dong Stadium to be surrounded by a larger complex, featuring hotels, shopping centres, hospitals, parks, and other amenities, as well as the Hung Vuong International Sports Complex.

The main sports stadium in Hanoi at the moment is the My Dinh National Stadium, which is the home of the country's national soccer team, and which also hosts concerts and athletics events.

That venue has a seated capacity of just over 40,000 – although this can be expanded to 50,000 if necessary – and was only opened in September 2003.

In terms of recent Legends Global activity, earlier this week the firm extended its tie-up with Beemok Sports & Entertainment, which runs tennis' top-tier Cincinnati Open in the US.

Legends Global continues as the partnership and sales leader for that US tournament.

It has also recently been unveiled as the owner's representative for the new ballpark – for which ground has not yet been broken – of the Kansas City Royals from North America's Major League Baseball.

Djokovic celebrates 'big win' on return to Basel
article_text:
Novak Djokovic pulled off a hard-fought comeback victory over Ugo Humbert on his first appearance in Basel for 15 years.

Battling in the final months of the year to keep alive his chances of qualifying for the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin, Djokovic celebrated what he viewed as a "big win" by overcoming Frenchman Ugo Humbert 4-6 6-3 6-4.

The men's record 24-time major winner blasted a forehand winner down the line to end the contest after two and a half hours.

It ensured Djokovic, 11th in the race to Turin, remains in the hunt for a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals, for which only the year's top eight performers qualify.

The 39-year-old beat great rival Roger Federer to win the Basel title in 2009, and had not played at the event since 2011.

"I was under attack from the very first point and had to weather the storm," Djokovic said.

"It's my first indoor match, so I expected to be a little bit rusty in a tough draw. It is a big win for me, I know there are quite a few things I can do better but a win is a win, and I will take that today."

This was Djokovic's 20th tour-level win of the year. It is the 21st consecutive season of his astonishing career in which he has achieved that tally.

After conceding the first set, Djokovic hung on against the 38th-ranked Humbert as he twice saved break points to escape an immediate setback in the second.

But the Serb, contesting his first indoor event since winning the Athens title last November, was solid from there, breaking Humbert's serve for the first time in the following game to kickstart his fightback.

Djokovic entered the tournament 319 points behind Spain's Rafael Jodar, who currently occupies the final ATP Finals qualification spot and also gained 50 points after coming through his first-round match.

Djokovic is also bidding to match Federer (103) for the second-most men's tour-level titles in the Open era in Basel, after ending a year-long wait for his 102nd title in Beijing in October.

Elsewhere, Great Britain's Harriet Dart progressed to the quarter-finals of the Guangzhou Open with a three-set victory over second seed Janice Tjen in China.

British number five Dart outlasted her Indonesian opponent as she prevailed 6-4 3-6 6-3 after two hours and 28 minutes.

Dart, ranked 115th in the world, will face former world number two Paula Badosa, after the Spaniard took just 67 minutes to beat Austria's Sinja Kraus 6-1 6-4.

title: 'Modern Approach To Sponsorship': NFL Opens Virtual In-Stadium Advertising To Brands On Madden NFL 27
article_text:
NFL has given the chance to official sponsors of its league partners and the 32 NFL clubs to purchase in-stadium advertising in the video game Madden NFL 27.

Thanks to EA SPORTS’ — the makers of the game — Madden NFL Virtual Stadium Sponsorship Program, sponsors have the opportunity to bring their real-world stadium presence into the matching Madden NFL stadiums, on console and mobile.

Pond Lehocky, work injury law firm and an Eagles partner, will be the first brand to take part. Its signage at Lincoln Financial Field will now appear in the Eagles’ stadium in Madden NFL.

By enabling NFL clubs to put their physical stadium signage into Madden NFL, the program makes the game’s venues more authentic to what fans see on game day. It also gives brands a new way to extend their existing sponsorships and reach millions of fans where they play, with signage that’s part of the stadium and doesn’t interrupt gameplay.

“Bringing real NFL stadium environments into Madden NFL makes game day feel more authentic while creating a natural extension of the sponsorships fans already see,” said Alex Dao, VP of advertising and sponsorships at Electronic Arts.

“It’s a clear example of how we’re building integrated brand opportunities with the player experience at the center, giving partners new ways to participate in sports fandom within the EA SPORTS ecosystem.”

Sponsor signage in Madden NFL stadiums is designed to reflect the real-world displays at NFL venues as more brands come on board.

Across console and mobile, fans play more than 2 billion Madden NFL games annually, the equivalent of 23,000 NFL seasons every day. That gives club partners significant visibility inside the stadiums where fans play.

“This program represents a modern approach to sports sponsorship by allowing our club partners to carry their physical stadium assets into the digital arena,” said Ed Kiang, vice president of interactive and experiential licensing at the NFL. “By extending club sponsorships into Madden, we’re creating a new way for brands to deepen their connection with NFL fans beyond game day.”

title: Leicester Tigers land major boost as England star agrees big-money new deal
article_text:
Leicester Tigers are set to secure the future of their club captain, with Ollie Chessum reportedly agreeing a new contract at Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

According to The Telegraph, the England international has signed a two-year extension that will keep him at the club beyond the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

The deal is reportedly worth more than £500,000 per season. Chessum has also been confirmed as Leicester's marquee player, meaning his salary will be exempt from the Premiership salary cap.

The agreement represents another significant boost for the Tigers as they look to retain their key players and build for the future.

Chessum began his professional career at Nottingham, making 11 appearances before joining Leicester in 2020.

He quickly established himself in the first team and played a crucial role in the club's 2022 Premiership title triumph.

His impressive performances earned him an England call-up, with the lock making his international debut against Italy in February 2022.

He went on to become a regular member of the national side, featuring at the 2023 Rugby World Cup as England secured third place.

Injuries disrupted his progress during 2023 and 2024, with an ankle problem followed by shoulder surgery.

However, Chessum returned to international action during the 2025 Six Nations before earning selection for the British and Irish Lions' tour of Australia.

He featured in all three Test matches, starting the second Test as the Lions clinched the series.

Leicester subsequently appointed Chessum as club captain in September 2025, recognising his growing influence both on and off the pitch.

His athleticism, lineout ability and powerful ball-carrying have made him an important figure for club and country.

The reported extension follows further positive contract news for Leicester, who have already confirmed that half-back duo Jack van Poortvliet and Billy Searle will remain at the club after their impressive recent form.

Chessum was also at the centre of the action during the East Midlands derby at the weekend, exchanging words with England team-mate Henry Pollock on several occasions as the players headed down the tunnel at half-time.

Leicester went into the break trailing but produced a dominant second-half display to turn the game around. The Tigers scored four unanswered tries to secure an emphatic 28-7 victory.

title: Dave Butcher confirmed permanent Scotland Women boss after interim spell
article_text:
Dave Butcher has been confirmed as the new permanent head coach of Scotland Women after a spell in interim charge.

He took over in the summer after the sudden departure of Sione Fukofuka and led the side through the WXV Global Series.

Although Scotland did not record a win during those five matches, and suffered heavy defeats to New Zealand and Canada, Scottish Rugby bosses have decided Butcher has done enough to earn the job on a long-term contract.

He will be in charge to at least the conclusion of the 2029 Women's Rugby World Cup.

Scottish Rugby performance director David Nucifora said: “Dave brings valuable experience across the international men’s and women’s game, with strong technical knowledge and a clear understanding of the demands of rugby at the highest level.

“Throughout a thorough appointment process, Dave demonstrated the coaching and leadership qualities we believe are important in taking the national team forward. His experience and collaborative approach give us confidence in his ability to lead the team.

“We look forward to continuing to support Dave and developing the coaching team around him as we build on the foundations in place and work towards sustained progress.”

Scottish Rugby also confirmed Butcher, whose family are currently living in Canada, will remain based in Scotland throughout his tenure.

On his permanent appointment, Butcher said: “It is fantastic to be named the Head Coach of Scotland Women. It is an amazing thing and group to be a part of.

“During my time in the role on an interim basis, I saw the work that was being done by Andy Rhys Jones and the vision from David Nucifora, and I knew I could add to it and wanted to be a part of driving that long-term.

“I’m really excited to be able to dive into the role beyond the recent campaign, focusing on the alignment of the programme and how we push forward performance from the National Talent Pathway, the National Academy, and the Celtic Challenge into the national team.

“We can’t be a standalone team without connection beneath us, so our immediate priority will be to review WXV and connect with the players, but going forward we want to be really intentional about how we go after our talent and how we develop that is going to be hugely important, with our rugby identity as a nation being key to all of that.”

Scottish Rugby Head of Women’s Performance and Pathways, Andy Rhys Jones, said: “I’m really pleased that Dave will lead Scotland Women as Head Coach on a permanent basis.

“Dave brings real quality as a coach, alongside the personal values and understanding of the culture needed to get the best out of players and staff. His approach to coaching and leadership will be important in driving the team forward.

“He understands the Scottish rugby landscape and the importance of working collaboratively across the national team and wider pathways system to support player development and prepare players to succeed at international level.

“Dave has a clear vision for Scotland Women and shares our ambition for the team. His appointment provides continuity and alignment as we work together to build a strong national team environment and achieve sustained progress and success.”

During his spell in interim charge, Butcher was assisted by Chris Laidlaw (defence) and Tom Luke, who was on secondment from Bristol Bears as attack coach.

With Luke now back at the PWR club, the process of recruiting a new attack coach will now begin.

title: Newport-born new WRU chairman Lyndon Faulkner vows he will not be a ‘yes man’
article_text:
Former Pontypool rugby star Lyndon Faulkner will not be a 'yes man' when he starts his role as chairman of the Welsh Rugby Union.

The Newport-born millionaire businessman and former rugby player, who does not officially start his role until next month, has already outlined his priorities, which include a review of the controversial plan to reduce Wales' professional clubs from four to three by 2028.

Faulkner, who is the nephew of Wales rugby legend Tony 'Charlie' Faulkner, has rejected claims that he was appointed to simply agree to the proposed changes.

He said: "There's talk out there that whoever took this job was under the condition that they can't talk about that [regional shake-up] but that's absolutely incorrect.

"I wouldn't have taken the job with those conditions or if it were me needing to be a yes man. That's not me."

Faulkner also admitted that he was not aware of the full extent of the WRU's debt until it was announced last week.

He stated: "I feel it's my role to review everything we've got going on, challenge it, probe it, and hopefully bring my experience to bear where I feel we can do things better."

When asked if he would be prepared to reverse the WRU's decision to cut a region, Faulkner replied: "Absolutely - and that's on anything I see."

Faulkner is a fan of any potential Anglo-Welsh competition, having played in a similar competition for Pontypool in the 1980s.

He broadly agreed with the WRU's decision to rescue Cardiff.

He will not be part of the WRU executive team but will chair the board, where he will wield significant influence.

"They picked me because of my experience so it would be foolish to not take consideration of what I say," he said.

Faulkner, who has a successful track record of turning around struggling businesses, expressed concern about the WRU's financial losses.

He said: "That was quite a surprise to me because the previous finances didn't look that bad, but they are worrying."

He believes that changes or improvements can be made to manage costs and increase revenue.

WRU loss soars to £18.1m despite £10.1m rise in revenue over the year to June

Faulkner, who was a centre in the formidable Pontypool team of the 1980s, said he was shaped by working under inspirational coach Ray Prosser.

He said: "He was an amazing man and there's a whole mix of emotions and things you learn under coaches like that.

"I've always believed in the skills rugby teaches you, not just on the field but teamwork, camaraderie, competition, winning."

Despite his successful business career, Faulkner's love for Welsh rugby is his main motivation in his new role.

"I love Welsh rugby and this is purely motivated around trying to make a difference.

"I can apply all the things I've done in business but as an ex-player, I also understand rugby."

title: Naomi Osaka stunned by 18-year-old Mia Pohankova at Pan Pacific Open in Japan
article_text:
Naomi Osaka's run at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo came to an end on Thursday after she suffered a surprise defeat against Slovakia's Mia Pohankova.

The seventh-seeded Osaka, playing in front of her home fans, lost 6-3, 7-5 to the 18-year-old wildcard entrant. The match lasted one hour and 35 minutes, with Pohankova booking her place in the quarterfinals.

Pohankova turned 18 just a week ago. She will next face Alycia Parks for a place in the semifinals. The Slovakian made a name for herself in junior tennis by winning the girls' singles title at Wimbledon in 2025.

Osaka had entered the second round on the back of a win over Jasmine Paolini in Tokyo. However, she could not continue her run against the young Slovakian.

Parks also secured a place in the quarterfinals on Thursday, defeating Australia's Kimberly Birrell 6-3, 6-1.

Canada's Leylah Fernandez produced another strong performance, beating fifth seed Elise Mertens 6-2, 7-6 (8) to move into the next round.

In a late match, top seed Elena Rybakina was scheduled to face Yulia Putintseva. Both players were born in Russia but represent Kazakhstan.

The tournament had already lost two seeded players due to injuries.

Second seed Maja Chwalinska withdrew with an injury to her left thigh, while fourth seed Belinda Bencic pulled out because of a right ankle injury.

title: Kieran Hardy: Ospreys and Wales scrum-half faces World Cup fitness race
article_text:
Wales scrum-half Kieran Hardy faces a race to be fit for next year's World Cup in Australia.

Hardy, 30, has had surgery this week after suffering a serious knee injury in the United Rugby Championship (URC) victory against Dragons at Rodney Parade.

Ospreys head coach Mark Jones has confirmed Hardy will miss the rest of the season but hopes Hardy can be fit in time for the World Cup which starts in October 2027.

"It is a serious knee injury which has needed surgery which tells you its extent," said Jones.

"It was a to major ligament of the knee and he has got some other bits and pieces that needed rectifying as well.

"We are definitely not going to see him this season, we just hope he has a good rehabilitation, there are no kinks in the road and everything goes to plan.

"We will be crossing everything that he is around for the start of the next season and his availability with the World Cup on the horizon."

Hardy has been a regular Wales deputy for Tomos Williams, while Ospreys team-mate Reuben Morgan-Williams and the uncapped Dragons number nine Che Hope have also been named in Steve Tandy's side for the Nations Championship in November.

Hardy has never played a World Cup game but was called up to the squad in the tournament in France as injury cover in 2023.

"That will be his target but you have to go with the speed the body lets you," said Jones.

"You have to have goals when you are out for a lengthy period and what better target than playing for your country at a World Cup.

"That is an awesome goal that will keep him on track. He is a great professional and he will apply himself.

"It is a huge carrot, and until somebody tells him that is not achievable, that is what he will be going for."

title: Shorts: Aurora Media Worldwide, Audi, Formula 1
article_text:
The Premier Jumping League (PJL), a new team-based showjumping competition backed by McCourt Global, has appointed Aurora Media Worldwide as its host broadcast production partner ahead of its first season in April 2027.

Under an initial three-year agreement, Aurora will produce the league’s international host broadcast feed, highlights programming and behind-the-scenes coverage across all nine events on its calendar, which covers North America, Europe and the Middle East.

The PJL will be distributed on a free-to-view model in its first season, a strategy it presented to the media rights industry at SPORTEL Monaco earlier this month. The league and Aurora plan to use broadcast technology, data capture and new production techniques to make showjumping and the PJL’s team format easier for first-time viewers to follow. The production will place greater emphasis on scale, sound and real-time sporting data.

The appointment sits alongside the PJL’s partnership with Box to Box Films, the production company behind Formula 1: Drive to Survive, which will produce content on the sport’s leading figures for audiences beyond the equestrian community.

The 16-team league is backed by McCourt Global and its Executive Chairman, Frank McCourt. It has committed $300m in guaranteed prize money across its first three seasons. The opening season begins in Las Vegas on 15th April 2027. International broadcast distribution partners will be announced later.

Part of Banijay Entertainment, Aurora produces live sport and original content for rights holders, broadcasters and brands. Its clients include Formula E, the E1 Series, the Barclays Women’s Super League, the LTA, the ICC and Baller League.

Lawrence Duffy, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Aurora, said, “We’re excited to work with the PJL team to create a distinctive broadcast product that combines world-class live production, innovative technology and compelling storytelling. Our ambition is not just to showcase the competition, but to help build the sport, bring fans closer to the riders and horses, and create a modern viewing experience across broadcast and digital platforms.”

Nikolaus von Doetinchem, Chief Commercial Officer at the PJL, said, “At the heart of every successful modern sports league is a world-class media product. How a sport is packaged and distributed is fundamental to its ability to engage audiences and achieve sustainable growth.

“Aurora has a proven track record of delivering broadcast production at the highest level, including its work with innovative sporting properties such as Formula E. Their experience in bringing emerging sports formats to global audiences aligns perfectly with the PJL’s ambition to modernise how showjumping is presented and experienced.”

Former Mercedes-AMG High Performance Powertrains Managing Director Thomas Fuhr will become CEO of Audi Formula Racing on 1st November, taking charge of the company that designs and builds the power unit for Audi’s Formula 1 team.

The appointment restructures AFR’s leadership. Stefan Dreyer, Chief Technology Officer, will now focus fully on the technical development of Audi’s F1 power unit. Christian Foyer, Chief Operating Officer, will continue to oversee operations at the company’s base in Neuburg an der Donau, Germany.

Fuhr has more than 30 years of engineering and leadership experience. From 2009 to 2012 he was Managing Director of Mercedes-AMG High Performance Powertrains. He then held senior executive roles at GROHE and LIXIL, and most recently was Chief Technology Officer of Georg Fischer Building Flow Solutions.

Founded in 2022, AFR develops and manufactures the full drivetrain for Audi’s Formula 1 entry, including the hybrid system and gearbox. It is based at Audi’s Neuburg site, 16km from the company’s Ingolstadt headquarters, which previously housed its DTM, Le Mans, Dakar Rally and Formula E programmes. A new building of around 3,000 square metres has expanded the site’s test facilities, and AFR runs more than 20 engine and component test benches there. The site holds three-star environmental certification from the FIA, the highest level under its guidelines.

Audi has competed in Formula 1 with its own factory team since 2026. Alongside Neuburg, the project operates from Hinwil in Switzerland, home of the Audi Revolut F1 Team, and from a UK Technology Centre in Bicester.

Jürgen Rittersberger, CFO of AUDI AG and Chairman of the Shareholders’ Meeting of Audi Formula Racing GmbH, said, “Audi’s Formula 1 project is a long-term strategic commitment and the continued development of our organization and leadership is fundamental to our ambitions. This appointment further strengthens the structure we have established at Audi Formula Racing.”

Mattia Binotto, CEO and Team Principal of the Audi Revolut F1 Team, said, “We have built strong foundations in Neuburg, developing Audi’s first Formula 1 power unit from the ground up. As Thomas understands both the technical challenge and what it takes to build and lead high-performing teams, I am confident he will play a key role by further developing the team and its organization to make us the best F1 manufacturer.”

Fuhr said, “The team in Neuburg has developed an entirely new power unit and brought it to the track. I want to build on that work by bringing together expertise across the organization and creating the conditions for us to compete at the highest level.”

Formula 1 has published its first sport-wide Social Impact Report and committed more than £2.4m to renew its Engineering Scholarship programme for a further three academic years, until 2028/29.

According to the report, more than 500,000 young people in 71 countries took part in Formula 1 programmes in 2025, covering education, STEM and pathways into the sport. It combines, for the first time, the activity of Formula 1, the FIA, all 10 teams and 24 race promoters during the 2025 season.

title: Singleton to play first game since heart issue as three set for Glasgow debuts
article_text:
Glasgow will field eight players released by Scotland in Friday’s URC clash with the Lions despite being without another 11 players retained by Gregor Townsend before their first November Nations Championship game against New Zealand next week.

Five of the released players – Ollie Smith, Stafford McDowall, George Horne, Alex Craig and Jamie Ritchie – will start the game at Scotstoun, with three more – Gregor Hiddleston, Max Williamson and Seb Stephen – deployed from the bench.

Head coach Franco Smith has also handed debuts to recent short-term signing Jack Singleton, the former Gloucester and England hooker whose last game was in September 2025 before suffering a heart attack and subsequently having stents fitted, and 20-year-old academy prop Jake Shearer.

Summer arrival Bayley Kuenzle will get a first competitive start on the wing after four outings off the bench, centre Johnny Ventisei will get a first senior outing of the season while another academy player, Cameron van Wyk, is poised for his debut off the bench.

Shearer’s inclusion is because Townsend has opted to retain Rory Sutherland ahead of the meeting with the All Blacks as well as fellow Glasgow loosehead Nathan McBeth, whose training has been restricted this week owing to an arm injury.

“He has just developed some pins and needles in his arm,” Smith reported. “That can be the cause of it or it can even be that he slept on that part of his neck wrongly. He didn’t train most of this week with Scotland and I think the precautionary decision was made.”

Smith is also without full-back Josh McKay, who qualifies for Scotland mid-way through the November programme and was rested for the past two matches, but who injured his hamstring while warming up with the team before their win against Benetton last week.

“I think he was over-keen and over-excited,” Smith explained. “In the last action of the warm-up, he just felt his hamstring, and that’s come back as a Grade 1B [minor strain or tear].

“It’s also a very light strain. Again, with the excitement, his name has been mentioned [for Scotland], and I think it’s important to keep him as fit as possible now and in the next weeks.”

New South African No.8 Ruwald van der Merwe has also sustained a hamstring strain.

“Funnily enough, for Ruwald, with the sudden drop in temperature, I think his normal warm-up routines from South Africa are not ones that he will be able to use here,” Smith said. “I think that maybe led to him tightening up in the last week. I don’t want to take a risk now of having a big injury so early in the season if we do push him. It’s just a very low-grade hamstring injury. Probably, if we played next week, he would have been fine.”

With two of Scotland’s three hookers, Gregor Hiddleston and Seb Stephen, both being utilised as replacements – Stephen possibly in a hybrid, ball-carrying back-row role – Singleton, 31, will get the chance to resume his career from the start.

“He’s been training so well and he’s so well prepared,” Smith said. “One of the things we want for this week is energy and enthusiasm, and he’s brought so much from that perspective.

“Having had the two players [Hiddleston and Stephen] involved with Scotland this whole week, it allowed us to give him the best chance to be prepared for a start.

“I’m excited to see what he can bring. He’s ready. You can just imagine how keen he is to get back into the mix.”

Singleton recently spoke about the heart issue that brought a halt to his career with Gloucester, who honoured his contract from last September until the summer but decided not to offer him a new deal beyond that point.

“It was a hereditary condition that we didn’t know about,” he revealed. “I had an angiogram. So I’ve had some stents and balloons inserted to help open up my arteries. And that was in September and then the follow-up [surgery] in December. And since the operations and procedures that I’ve had, and the drugs that I’m now taking, everything’s more under control. So I’m in a much safer spot than I was 16 months ago when I was playing.”

Smith also addressed this week’s abrupt departure of assistant coach Roddy Grant following an internal disciplinary process.

Grant, who worked predominantly with the forwards on the breakdown and contact, will not be replaced, with Smith preferring to share the workload with his chief lieutenants Nigel Carolan (attack) and Scott Forrest (defence) and assorted academy coaches.

“Obviously we’re disappointed with everything that happened, but that’s that,” Smith said. “It wasn’t a difficult situation at all. It was well dealt with by [Warriors managing director] Kenny Brown, and from his leadership perspective, we carried on.

“We’ve coached without another assistant coach before. I prefer it that way in a certain way, and we were always thinking Roddy would add value to his coaching career by involving him.

“It was always just myself and [former defence coach] Pete Murchie and Nigel Carolan in the beginning. So it’s back to me being with Scott and Nigel, and then I’ve got all the assistants, from [academy coaches] Shane Munro and Duncan Weir to [scrum coach] Alasdair Dickinson.

“So, we have enough people around. Everybody knows what they’re doing. I think the opportunity was there to enhance another coach, and that didn’t work out. But we have more than enough.

title: Wales name changed line-up for Japan Test as Keira Bevan drops to bench
article_text:
Wales head coach Sean Lynn has made five changes to his starting XV as Wales aim for back-to-back wins for the first time since 2023.

Alex Callender and Kate Williams continue to captain the side from the back-row, although Callender will start this fixture at No. 8. Bethan Lewis starts at openside flanker.

Elsewhere in the pack, Gwenllian Pyrs starts ahead of Maisie Adams at loosehead prop. Kelsey Jones and Sisilia Tuipulotu continue in the front-row. Gwen Crabb is drafted in at lock forward to partner Branwen Metcalfe.

Courtney Keight is installed at inside centre after Freya Bell was ruled out of the fixture with a knee injury. The Sale Sharks back partners Carys Cox in the midfield.

It is at half-back where Lynn has made his biggest call. Lleucu George is named at fly-half, where she partners scrum-half Seren Lockwood. Keira Bevan is named among the replacements and can cover both positions.

Sean Lynn, Wales head coach, said: “We have made the changes to reward the players who finished the job in Tokyo, and they deserve the opportunity to start for their country for our final Test match of 2026.

“The players know our DNA is team first and competition for places drives standards and performances and will only help us improve and get better as a team.

“We are obviously disappointed with the injury to Freya Bell, but she will get the best care and supervision by the WRU staff, and we hope to see her back soon.

“We found a way in the first Test in Tokyo and the way the players problem-solved during the game was key for all the coaches.

“But we know we have to be much more accurate and produce a consistent 80-minute performance to beat a resilient Japan side that we know will be hurting.

“We need to back up what we achieved in the first Test and sign off the 11-week block we have been together and this WXV campaign on a high in Kumagaya.”

title: England's Atkinson stays at Gloucester until 2029
article_text:
England centre Seb Atkinson has signed a new contract to extend his time with Gloucester until at least 2029.

The 24-year-old had options to leave the club, according to head coach George Skivington, but chose to stay with the current Prem leaders.

"This is a really significant re-signing for us," Skivington said.

"Seb had plenty of options on the table, so his commitment to the club is a real indication of where Gloucester Rugby is right now.

"Seb has been exceptional for us since the day he arrived. He came with great physical qualities and an outstanding level of professionalism in the way he approaches his own development and the success of the team."

Atkinson joined Gloucester from Worcester in 2022 and has become one of their most influential players in recent seasons, starting 79 of the 84 games he has played for the club.

He won his first England cap in July 2025 and has gone on to play seven times for his country.

"There's no doubt the faith the coaches have shown in me and the time they've invested in my development has played a huge role in shaping the player and person I am today," Atkinson said.

"Playing at Kingsholm is a privilege, and I've been overwhelmed by how the Gloucester supporters have welcomed me and made me feel one of their own.

"I'm in a place where I feel valued by the coaches, the fans and my team-mates. I'm enjoying my rugby and feel this is the perfect environment for me to continue developing and improving my game.

"Most importantly, I'm committed to helping bring success to this club. When I took all of those things into consideration, signing a new deal was the only decision."

title: Roger Federer confirms special comeback as Joao Fonseca dream set to come true
article_text:
Joao Fonseca looks set to have his wish granted as Roger Federer has confirmed he will head to Brazil for a special event.

At the French Open, Fonseca admitted he is a huge Federer fan and wished the Swiss was regarded as the greatest player of all time, before conceding that Novak Djokovic gets that honour.

Earlier this week, the 20-year-old, who ended his season prematurely due to injury, admitted it was a long-held dream of his to play with the 20-time Grand Slam winner one day.

He said, via Globo, “Without a doubt, the person I’d most like to hit a ball with is Roger Federer. He’s always been an inspiration to me, both on and off the court. Just hitting a few balls with him would be a dream.”

On 12 December, the Brazilian is set to play Carlos Alcaraz in an exhibition in Sao Paulo, and now, Federer has announced that he is coming to the same city for another tennis event.

In an Instagram video, after Fonseca asked the 45-year-old if he is coming to Brazil, Federer is heard saying, “Hey, Joao. Well, I guess the secret is out now.

“I am finally coming back to Brazil after all these years, and this December we will meet at Clubhouse Nights in São Paulo. See you on the court, my friend.”

Brazilian rising star Fonseca added, “Let’s go for it!”

According to Globo, Fonseca and Federer will play tennis together during the event on 5 December but the game will be different from the ‘traditional’ format, with music and entertainment thrown in as well.

Fonseca is sponsored by Federer’s Swiss sportswear brand ‘On’, which is a big reason why this event is taking place. title: Pan Pacific Open: Naomi Osaka stunned by 18-year-old Mia Pohankova and knocked out in front of home crowd in Tokyo
article_text:
Naomi Osaka, seeded No 7 and playing before home fans in Japan, was knocked out of the Pan Pacific Open on Thursday by teenager Mia Pohankova.

Slovakia's Pohankova, who turned 18 a week ago and was a wild-card entry in Japan, upset Osaka 6-3 7-5 to advance to the quarter-finals.

Pohankova will face Alycia Parks in the last eight.

Pohankova, the 2025 junior singles champion at Wimbledon, stunned Osaka, who was coming off a win over Jasmine Paolini in the first round in Tokyo.

In other round-of-16 matches on Thursday, Parks defeated Kimberly Birrell 6-3 6-1, and Leylah Fernandez defeated No 5 Elise Mertens 6-2 7-6 (8-6).

In a late match, top-ranked Elena Rybakina will face Yulina Putintseva. Both were born in Russia but represent Kazakhstan.

Second-seeded Maja Chwalinska and No. 4 Belinda Bencic pulled out of the tournament earlier with injuries. Chwalinska has an injured left thigh and Bencic has a right-ankle injury.

title: Aurora lands Premier Jumping League host broadcast contract
article_text:
The Premier Jumping League (PJL), the new global showjumping competition due to launch next year, has appointed Aurora Media Worldwide as its host broadcast production partner ahead of its inaugural 2027 season.

Under a three-year agreement, Aurora will lead the production of the PJL's international host broadcast feed, highlights programming, and behind-the-scenes coverage across all nine events on the league's global calendar, which spans North America, Europe, and the Middle East.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The PJL will be free-to-view as part of the league’s strategy to provide “ease of access” during its inaugural season as it seeks to build a “more globally diverse fanbase.”

Nikolaus von Doetinchem, chief commercial officer at the PJL, said: “At the heart of every successful modern sports league is a world-class media product. How a sport is packaged and distributed is fundamental to its ability to engage audiences and achieve sustainable growth.

“Aurora has a proven track record of delivering broadcast production at the highest level, including its work with innovative sporting properties such as Formula E. Their experience in bringing emerging sports formats to global audiences aligns perfectly with the PJL’s ambition to modernise how showjumping is presented and experienced.

“This partnership represents an important step in our commitment to transforming the sport’s broadcast proposition, showcasing its extraordinary athleticism, sporting jeopardy and the emotional connection between horse and rider to a new generation of fans.”

Starting in April 2027, the PJL will feature 16 teams competing across 14 international venues, with the competition aiming to create a sustainable economic model via a centralized sponsorship and broadcasting model. The events will involve top riders, including world number one Scott Brash.

The PJL issued a tender for a host broadcast partner in May, two months after the league announced it would launch with a guaranteed prize pot of $300 million.

The league is backed by McCourt Global, the investment firm of American billionaire and prolific sports team owner Frank McCourt, who previously held a 50% stake in the premium show jumping series, the Global Champions Tour, and founded the show jumping team, the Miami Celtics.

McCourt, who is named as founder and chairman of PJL, currently owns French soccer club Olympique de Marseille, but previously owned baseball’s iconic Los Angeles Dodgers.

To help attract new audiences, the league has partnered with production company Box to Box Films, the producers of the popular Formula 1 motor racing series 'Drive to Survive'.

The $300 million on offer across the 14 events is one of the biggest investments in an equestrian competition.

By comparison, show jumping’s top-tier Global Tour distributed €22 million across its final flagship events last year, the Global Champions Tour and Global Champions League finals in Riyadh, as well as the Global Champions Prague Playoffs.

Specifically, €10.5 million was distributed across the 2025 LGCT and GCL Season Championships in Riyadh, which featured the world’s best athletes, while the GC Prague Playoffs saw a prize fund of more than €11.4 million split between the GCL Super Cup (€10 million) and GC Tour Super Grand Prix (€1.25 million).

Lawrence Duffy, founder and chief executive of Aurora, added: “The PJL is exactly the kind of ambitious global sports property we love working with. There is a huge opportunity to bring the spectacle, athleticism, and drama of elite showjumping to a much wider audience.

“We're excited to work with the PJL team to create a distinctive broadcast product that combines world-class live production, innovative technology, and compelling storytelling.

“Our ambition is not just to showcase the competition, but to help build the sport, bring fans closer to the riders and horses, and create a modern viewing experience across broadcast and digital platforms.”

title: Aussie businesses pouring tens of millions into future sport stars
article_text:
Harvey Norman has long been a pioneer backer of female sport including sponsoring athletes from Olympian Ariarne Titmus and Paralympian Madison de Rozario to rugby league trailblazer Ali Brigginshaw.

Asked what underpinned the Gerry Harvey-founded Harvey Norman’s longstanding backing of Australian sport, the homeware and technology retail giant’s chief executive Katie Page said it stemmed back to a Queensland teacher identifying she was gifted as an 11 year old.

“A teacher said to my parents ‘Your daughter should go to this particular school’. It’s just having that person who was supporting me and saying ‘You’ve got something’,” she said.

“So I often think back to these young athletes how important it is – and we do scholarships for Western Sydney university too – that we do a lot of things that say to these young women ‘You’ve got someone that believes in you’.”

De Rozario, a champion 800-metre and marathon wheelchair racer who has competed at two Paralympics and four Commonwealth Games, said corporate backing doing “the heavy lifting” for athletes is a “game changer” for performance.

De Rozario said: “It makes a big difference. As athletes, we get very caught up in what we are doing and our high performance, our daily training environment and you forget the impact sport has on the community until you get out there and you do pull on the green and gold. Then you realise how many people’s eyes are on screens and are emotionally invested in what we are doing.

“Corporate backing, the Harvey Norman support, it intertwines into all of that. It kind of does so much of the heavy lifting.”

Michelle Klein, Westpac’s Chief Growth, Brand and Marketing Officer, said sport sponsorships were a key part of the bank’s strategy.

Westpac has had a long association with the NRL, Queensland Rugby League and NSW Rugby League.

The bank has also taken over as the main sponsor of the Australian men’s and women’s cricket team, with that deal now in its second year.

“Australia is sports mad and such an integral part of our culture,” she said.

Westpac’s program also supported grassroots sports through the Her Games Grows campaign, which encouraged girls and women to play cricket at all levels, she added.

Qantas’ Chief brand and Corporate Affairs Officer Danielle Keighery said: “Sport is a big part of who we are as a nation and a source of pride for millions of Australians. Qantas is proud to play a part, helping our athletes get where they need to go as they represent Australia at home and around the world.”

The Back Australia series is supported by Harvey Norman, Ampol, Bunnings, Qantas, AAMI, Journey Beyond, Gippsland Critical Minerals and News24.

title: Gloucester Rugby see off interest from Leicester Tigers, Saracens and Harlequins to secure vice-captain
article_text:
Gloucester Rugby have seen off considerable competition from the likes of Leicester Tigers, Saracens and Harlequins to agree a contract extension with England international Seb Atkinson in a massive boost for the table-topping club.

Atkinson, still just 24, joined the Cherry and Whites from Worcester Warriors in 2022 and quickly established himself as a fan favourite thanks to his physicality on both sides of the ball, relentless work rate and consistency of performance, becoming vice captain of the club in the last couple of years.

His impact in Cherry & White has been recognised with a number of accolades, including being named Stowford Press Supporters' Player of the Year in both 2023/24 and 2025/26.

Most notably, he earned his first senior England cap against Argentina in 2025 and has since established himself as a regular in Steve Borthwick's setup to be awarded an Enhanced Elite Player Squad contract with the national side. He was recently named in the squad for the upcoming Nations Championship campaign.

Atkinson’s extension will see him remain with the Kingsholm until at least 2029.

Gloucester head coach George Skivington, said: "This is a really significant re-signing for us. Seb had plenty of options on the table, so his commitment to the club is a real indication of where Gloucester Rugby is right now.

"Seb has been exceptional for us since the day he arrived. He came with great physical qualities and an outstanding level of professionalism in how he approaches his own development and the team's success.

"He's the ultimate professional and a fantastic role model for any young rugby player in the way he carries himself on matchdays, in training and away from the field.

"We're delighted to get Seb's deal over the line and look forward to him remaining a key part of what we're building at Gloucester Rugby for many years to come.”

Atkinson added: "I'm really grateful to the Club for everything they've given me since arriving at Kingsholm. There's no doubt the faith the coaches have shown in me, and the time they've invested in my development, has played a huge role in shaping the player and person I am today.

"Playing at Kingsholm is a privilege, and I've been overwhelmed by how the Gloucester supporters have welcomed me and made me feel one of their own.

"I'm in a place where I feel valued by the coaches, the fans and my teammates. I'm enjoying my rugby and feel this is the perfect environment for me to continue developing and improving my game.

"Most importantly, I'm committed to helping bring success to this Club. When I took all of those things into consideration, signing a new deal was the only decision.”

title: NZR endorses Super Rugby Pacific and NPC as right path for men’s competitions
article_text:
New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has today confirmed the direction of the country’s elite men’s rugby competition and streamlined player pathways that underpin it.

Currently, Super Rugby Pacific and the NPC operate as New Zealand’s two men’s competitions, supported by 19 professional rugby environments across five Super Rugby clubs and 14 Provincial Unions.

The changes confirm Super Rugby Pacific and the NPC as the right competitions to support the continued success of the All Blacks, develop players and excite fans.

NZR and Rugby Australia will work together alongside Super Rugby clubs and the respective players associations to transform how Super Rugby Pacific engages fans, attracts investors and generates revenue.

The NPC will remain a strong 14-team provincial competition that is critical to building depth, connecting rugby to the regions and providing pathways for players across the country.

The Super Rugby and Provincial Union operations in the same five cities will be consolidated to drive better community rugby, high performance and financial outcomes.

The nine regional NPC Provincial Unions will have stronger relationships with their Super Rugby clubs, supported by strengthened pathway protections to ensure talented players can develop in their home regions and stay connected with their communities.

With the direction approved by the Board, NZR will now begin working with its key rugby stakeholders to develop the changes ahead of a final NZR Board decision. Implementation is expected from 2028.

“New Zealanders should be proud of what sets us apart as a rugby nation, being the layers in our game from club and school to the NPC, Super Rugby and the All Blacks.

“We are making changes to our game from a position of strength, and we have two men’s competitions that support the All Blacks to win, excite fans and players and, with these changes, can be financially successful.

“Together with our stakeholders, we’re now focused on improving the way Super Rugby Pacific engages fans, continuing to strengthen the NPC and ensuring talented players can develop in a clear, aligned pathway.”

Lancaster added that Super Rugby Pacific needed more ambition and bold thinking to transform the competition.

“We’re aligned with Rugby Australia and the Super Rugby clubs that we need people who wake up every day focused on engaging fans, growing revenue and working with broadcasters and the media. We’re open to working on things like player movement, a competition-wide salary cap and centralising commercial assets across the key markets. Those are conversations we will now have with Rugby Australia, the Rugby Players Association and the Super Rugby clubs. We know it’s a great product on the field and it now needs to generate the level of attendance and revenue that it warrants.”

“One of the most important factors in developing players the All Blacks want to select is having competitions that excite players and energise our fans.

“For 30 years, Super Rugby has proven to a great competition that meets a key high performance principle which is to ensure that our best players are playing with and against each other more often. The NPC is equally as critical to ensuring that our pipeline of talented players maintains its depth through 14 teams.”

“The NPC is absolutely the jewel in New Zealand rugby’s pathway and provides opportunities for players wherever they are in the country. It keeps our playing base wide and is critical to player, coach and referee development.

“While these changes will reduce duplication and cost, more importantly they simplify rugby operations and player pathways in our major cities and ensure we are operating as one team from community rugby through to the All Blacks.

“We want the community and professional game working as one, with a single, clear pathway for talented school leavers into professional and international rugby.”

Collins added that with Super Rugby Pacific set to become more independent from NZR day-to-day management, the organisation could prioritise NPC more, including promotion.

The changes form part of work NZR recently began with its stakeholders to reduce costs across the sport by 5 percent and create a $20m annual improvement from 2028.

As well as men’s and women’s competitions, NZR is also reviewing how community rugby is delivered across the country, and NZR’s own structure and operations.

The aim is to allow NZR to invest more into the community game and ensure competitions attract fans, are financially successful and keep professional players and coaches in New Zealand.

title: ‘You Get Fitter by Suffering’: Jack Draper on Training, Recovery and His Road Back from Injury
article_text:
Jack Draper is in a reflective mood, as he continues to work his way back from the long-term arm injury that has kept him out of competitive tennis.

What started as pins and needles in his arm became increasingly painful before scans revealed serious bone stress. The recovery has been complicated, not least because a tennis player can't simply stop using the arm that's causing the problem.

But sitting down with him, it becomes clear the injury has changed more than his physical preparation.

Draper has spent most of his life being a tennis player. Now, for the first time, he's had to work out who he is when he isn't playing.

That's meant taking recovery more seriously, adapting his training and finding time for things he'd largely neglected – friends, family, holidays, even gardening. He's also developed a different perspective on what success actually means.

Draper recently announced a long-term partnership with Scandinavian recovery technology brand Flowlife, which he had already been using during his rehabilitation. Recovery has become a much bigger part of his routine, alongside strength and conditioning, nutrition and sleep.

Here, Draper talks openly about the physical and mental demands of elite tennis – and what he's learnt while being forced to step away from it.

Men's Health: You've had to step away from competing just as your hard work was really starting to pay off. How do you keep that sense of progress going when you're not able to compete?

Jack Draper: It was difficult to deal with. In 2022, when I first came onto tour, I broke the top 100, which is every tennis player's dream. In 2023, I was injured a fair bit but finished the year around 40 in the world.

Then in 2024 and halfway through 2025, I was really climbing the rankings and feeling unbelievable in myself and my body. All my hard work and sacrifices were paying off. And all of a sudden I got hit with a really difficult, complicated injury.

I really tried for a long, long time to work for it and keep going. I'd worked so hard to get to where I was, so I was desperate. Especially in tennis, you're kind of watching yourself falling every week, trying to not let the boat sink.

I think it's been more about taking myself away from the game a little bit to get my energy back.

I started playing and working when I was about 16, so all I've ever known is my tennis. I've probably neglected a lot of other areas of my life, like going on holiday or meeting friends and just doing normal things.

So I suppose it's helped me realise that success isn't just tennis. Success can be feeling good in yourself. Success can be having great relationships with the people that you love around you and taking time for that as well.

JD: It was a weird one. I was in Madrid last year, I made the final there, and during that week I practised a couple of times and felt like I had pins and needles in my arm. Those pins and needles became more frequent when I was playing and practising.

Then it got to the point where the French Open and Queen's started getting quite a sharp pain in my bicep.

As a tennis player, you're constantly using your body. You might be dealing with two, three, four different niggles at the same time, so you kind of just play through it.

When I got it scanned after Wimbledon, they said I'd had quite serious bone stress in my arm. I didn't know what that meant at all. I was thinking, ‘Oh, it's just going to be six weeks, that'll be good.’

Unfortunately, it doesn't work like that with a bone, especially because they don't heal easily. I have to use my arm all the time when I'm hitting the ball.

And there's a lot of complexity because there are different areas around that arm. It's not just the bone. The bone causes inflammation, which then maybe causes bicep tendinitis, maybe causes elbow problems, maybe causes a nerve problem.

It was my first experience of chronic pain and it's difficult because you start not thinking of yourself as an athlete. You start thinking of yourself just as a normal person. You start wanting to feel OK in yourself again.

MH: Talk us through the recovery process.

JD: There's lots of peaks and troughs. The first six to eight months, I was in pain all the time, more so when I was playing.

The difficult thing with bones is people will say, ‘I'm going to take a break, just stop playing.’ It doesn't work like that. I think it's because the bone needs to keep getting turned over to adapt, especially to the sport I play.

The injury improves itself when you change your biomechanics, when you change the way your body's working to be more efficient, instead of just taking a break.

So as I was getting better, especially this year, it was about changing my biomechanics, changing potentially the stiffness of my racket and my strings and all those sorts of things.

MH: Has the injury changed your mindset?

JD: I think I was at that level of just fighting for it for so long that I almost needed a bit of a break from it all.

title: USGA Chief Gives Big Tiger Woods Senior Open Hint
article_text:
The pursuit of more golfing history is the reason Tiger Woods is being backed to play in the US Senior Open.

We're back in the full swing of wondering when Woods will play again following his latest long-term absence from the game, resulting from injury and that infamous car crash in Florida in March which led to him receiving a five-year driving ban.

The 15-time Major champion hasn't played a professional tourmanent since the 2024 Open Championship but has been spotted making swings on the range at the TGR Junior Invitational at Pebble Beach recently as he prepares for his latest comeback.

Having turned 50, many believe his best route back into full competition is on the PGA Tour Champions and in the senior Majors - with the US Open offering a particular historical significance for Woods.

Next year's US Senior Open Championship at Oak Tree National in June may be a bit soon for Woods if his recovery is slow, but it's also starts 11 days after the end of the regular US Open at Pebble Beach - which will surely be a target for Woods.

Knowing Woods he's likely to feel he can still compete with the young guns in 2027, but he's been tipped to appear at the 2028 edition at Crooked Stick.

USGA’s Chief Championships Officer John Bodenhamer told local outlet WISH-TV News that he expected to see Woods at Crooked Stick in 2028 due to his relentless pursuit of golfing history.

Woods could break a tie with Bobby Jones for the all-time lead on nine USGA national titles, while he could also match Jack Nicklaus and Arnold Palmer by adding the US Senior Open to his CV.

But with Woods also winning the US Junior Amateur, US Amateur and US Open, adding the Senior Open would create a new slice of golfing history as the only man to win all four.

“Tiger understands his legacy," Bodenhamer told the local WISH-TV News. "Bob Jones won nine USGA national championships. Tiger Woods has won nine, and to win that tenth, if he could do it at the US Senior Open, he understands what that means.

“There’s only been two people in the history of our game that have won the US Amateur, the US Open, and the US Senior Open - Jack Nicklaus and Arnold Palmer.

"Tiger’s won the Am and the Open. He’s never won the Senior Open. But Tiger’s also won the Junior Am. He’d be the only one ever to do it.

“So I guess what I’m trying to say is, it’s important to Tiger, and I would expect that he would be here at Crooked Stick.”

Woods is looking to play a full TGL schedule in the upcoming season, while the PNC Championship could be a tournament return spot playing alongside son Charlie.

But for continuing his career in the medium to long term, the senior circuit and senior Majors seem to be the best path should Woods want to keep on competing.

Paul Higham is a sports journalist with over 20 years of experience in covering most major sporting events for both Sky Sports and BBC Sport. He is currently freelance and covers the golf majors on the BBC Sport website. Highlights over the years include covering that epic Monday finish in the Ryder Cup at Celtic Manor and watching Rory McIlroy produce one of the most dominant Major wins at the 2011 US Open at Congressional. He also writes betting previews and still feels strangely proud of backing Danny Willett when he won the Masters in 2016 - Willett also praised his putting stroke during a media event before the Open at Hoylake. Favourite interviews he's conducted have been with McIlroy, Paul McGinley, Thomas Bjorn, Rickie Fowler and the enigma that is Victor Dubuisson. A big fan of watching any golf from any tour, sadly he spends more time writing about golf than playing these days with two young children, and as a big fair weather golfer claims playing in shorts is worth at least five shots. Being from Liverpool he loves the likes of Hoylake, Birkdale and the stretch of tracks along England's Golf Coast, but would say his favourite courses played are Kingsbarns and Portrush.
