title: McKibbin announces switch from LIV Golf to DP World Tour
article_text:
TOM McKibbin is set to play a full season on the DP World Tour in 2027 after announcing his departure from LIV Golf.

The Holywood native joins former world number one Jon Rahm, fivetime Ryder Cup winner Ian Poulter and compatriot Graeme McDowell in quitting the breakaway league.

Although McKibbin raised a few eyebrows when he turned down a PGA Tour card to join Rahm’s Legion XIII team for the 2025 season, he went on to pocket just under $19 million from 26 events.

However, the Public Investment Fund – the sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia – withdrew its funding for LIV Golf in April.

That was followed by the league filing for bankruptcy in September, and the high-profile player exits have been coming thick and fast since then.

A new, privately-backed successor has recently been announced, known as LIV 2.0, and it is believed enough golfers have signed up, potentially enabling it to get off the ground.

Amidst an air of uncertainty, McKibbin’s decision to make to switch to the DP World Tour could have been encouraged by a number of motivating factors.

He previously signed a conditional release deal with DP, enabling him to play in seven tournaments on the European Tour, alongside fulfilling his LIV commitments.

Top-10 placings in the British Masters, Irish Open and India Championship have earned him a spot in the Race to Dubai’s top 100, which will allow the rising star to retain his card in the new year.

European Tour Group and Ryder Cup Europe CEO Guy Kinnings could also have forced his hand, making it clear that golfers must choose between LIV and DP, while the next Ryder Cup being held in Ireland could have influenced the decision to play in Europe.

Announcing his LIV departure, McKibbin said: “After two seasons with Legion XIII, I have decided not to sign with LIV Golf for its next chapter. I Will be playing a full schedule on the DP World Tour in 2027.”

“Joining LIV Golf was the right decision for me at the time, and I’m grateful for everything it has given me.

“Playing alongside Jon (Rahm), Tyrell (Hatton) and Caleb taught me more than I could have imagined. Thank you to them, the team staff and everyone at LIV Golf for making me feel at home from day one.

“I’ve taken time to think about what’s best for me and I am confident this is the right decision to help me achieve my goals.”

title: All Blacks great Jerome Kaino set to join World Cup rivals
article_text:
All Blacks great Jerome Kaino could be heading to the 2027 Rugby World Cup in a coaching role with a nation other than New Zealand.

According to Midi Olympique, the Toulouse coach is close to joining Georgia’s coaching staff, adding international duties to his existing position with the French giants.

An agreement between Toulouse and the Georgian Rugby Union has reportedly been finalised following several weeks of discussions.

Kaino is expected to join the Lelos for their November fixtures, with the possibility of remaining involved through to the 2027 World Cup already under consideration.

The former New Zealand international will reportedly focus on contact tactics and attacking rucks, bringing his experience at the highest level to Georgia’s forward play.

They face Canada, Tonga and the USA in this autumn's Nations Cup campaign.

He will work alongside new head coach Pierre-Henry Broncan, who took charge during the summer after Marco Bortolami’s interim spell, which followed Richard Cockerill’s departure.

The pair are already familiar with each other, having worked together at Toulouse in 2018, when Kaino was still playing and Broncan was the club's defence coach.

Georgia will face a significant challenge at the 2027 Rugby World Cup, having been drawn alongside South Africa, Italy and Romania in the pool stage.

Currently ranked 13th in the world, the Lelos will be targeting a place in the round of 16, with Kaino potentially playing an important role in their preparations.

Kaino established himself as one of the outstanding back-row forwards of his generation during a decorated career with New Zealand.

Born in American Samoa, he moved to Auckland at the age of four and switched from rugby league to union during his school years.

He made his Auckland debut in 2004 before earning his first All Blacks cap later that year, scoring a try against the Barbarians.

By 2008, Kaino had become New Zealand’s first-choice blindside flanker.

He played a major role in their 2011 Rugby World Cup triumph, scoring four tries during the tournament, before helping them retain the Webb Ellis Cup in 2015.

Following spells with Toyota Verblitz in Japan and the Blues, where he made 137 appearances, Kaino joined Toulouse in 2018.

He enjoyed further success in France, winning two Top 14 titles and the European Rugby Champions Cup before retiring as a player in 2021.

Kaino subsequently joined Toulouse’s coaching staff and remains with the club, with a potential international role in Georgia now offering him the chance to return to the Rugby World Cup stage in a different capacity.

title: Franco Smith addresses Roddy Grant Glasgow Warriors exit over disciplinary issue
article_text:
Franco Smith admits he was ‘disappointed’ with Roddy Grant’s conduct which led to the assistant coach being sacked.

In a succinct statement on Tuesday, Glasgow confirmed that the 39-year-old had departed Scotstoun after an 'internal process'. No further details have been made available about the circumstances of Grant's departure.

Scotland Rugby News understands the off-field incident wasn’t related to coaching with Glasgow deciding not to replace Grant for the remainder of the 2026/27 campaign.

While Smith wouldn’t comment on the disciplinary process, the Glasgow Warriors head coach stressed the importance of the culture around the club and his ingrained values, on and off the pitch.

“Look, the process was followed and we're just going to stick to the task and carry on each week," said Smith.

"Obviously we’re disappointed with everything that happened, but that's that. I think the club dealt with it and we're now heading on to the next thing. That is the way we've approached it.”

Asked if he felt let down by Grant, Smith added: “Look, we're a tight ship here and everybody knows exactly what my values are and where we stand and how we do things here. The culture of the club has been tried and tested over the last five years, and it comes up flying. That is what I'm proud of.

“This incident didn't influence anything that we did or do or want to become, or want to do, and the type of messaging that we give to the players. So, no, I think we weren't disrupted.

“Again, I think we wanted to give another person an opportunity to be involved in this environment and grow their coaching career. It's not what we can get, it's what we can give, and that was the approach.”

Former Edinburgh captain Grant was appointed by Glasgow Warriors in June 2025, alongside Scott Forrest, to replace Peter Murchie.

It’s no great surprise that Glasgow have decided against directly replacing Grant as Smith has complete faith in defence-coach Forrest and the highly-regarded attacking mastermind, Nigel Carolan.

Asked about the decision not to replace Grant, Smith added: “I think it was always just myself and Pete Murchie and Nigel Carolan in the beginning.

“So that’s me back to being with Pete and Nigel, and then I've got all the assistants, from Shane Munro and Duncan Weir to Alasdair Dickinson.

“So, we have enough people around. I think the opportunity was there to enhance another coach, and that didn't work out now. But we have more than enough.

“During the first three years, we just coached, the three of us. My dream was always about creating an opportunity for somebody else also to be a part of it and learn, and maybe progress somebody else as well, and now that it's just back to us, the workload is shared evenly. Everybody knows what they're doing.

“Again, we've got assistant coaches. It's not just one area of the game that can now be lacking. We are very happy with the people that we've got at the moment.”

title: Wales make five changes as Lynn rewards bench
article_text:
Wales have made five starting changes for Saturday's second WXV Test against Japan.

Flanker Bethan Lewis will make her first start of the campaign, having been one of Wales' impressive impact players in last weekend's 17-0 victory in Tokyo, with co-captain Alex Callender moving to number eight.

Gwen Crabb and Gwenllian Pyrs are also promoted from the bench to join the pack, while Lleucu George is preferred to Keira Bevan at fly-half.

George will partner Seren Lockwood, who crossed for two tries last weekend, as Wales seek back-to-back wins (07:00 GMT).

Courtney Keight comes in for centre Freya Bell, who looks set for a lengthy lay-off after suffering a serious knee injury in the opening Test.

Head coach Sean Lynn has again opted for six forwards and two backs on the bench.

"We have made the changes to reward the players who finished the job in Tokyo," said Lynn.

Wales are looking to finish their WXV campaign on a high at Kumagaya Rugby Stadium, having previously beaten Japan and South Africa and narrowly lost to USA.

They are ranked 11th in the world after overtaking Saturday's opponents with last week's victory.

"The players know our DNA is 'team first'. Competition for places drives standards and performances and will only help us improve and get better as a team," Lynn added.

"We are obviously disappointed with the injury to Freya Bell, but she will get the best care and we hope to see her back soon."

While last weekend was another welcome win for Lynn, Wales made hard work of the victory in testing conditions.

"We found a way in the first Test in Tokyo and the way the players problem-solved during the game was key for all the coaches," said Lynn.

"But we know we have to be much more accurate and produce a consistent, 80-minute performance to beat a resilient Japan side that we know will be hurting."

title: Why Friday? Fiji Rugby Union chief tells
article_text:
Why Friday? Fiji Rugby Union chief tells

The Flying Fijians coach will name his final Nations Championship squad after evaluating players during a three-day camp in France.

Flying Fijians head coach Jakes White shows Jiuta Wainiqolo how it's done while Seta Turagacoke looks on during training in Lyon, France, on October 27, 2026.

The Fiji Water-sponsored Flying Fijians’ final squad will be announced tomorrow to give head coach Jake White more time to assess the players.

Fiji Rugby Union chief executive officer Kali Sewabu told SUNsports yesterday that White needed more time to evaluate the squad.

White and 10 players from the Flying Fijians squad that beat Japan 34-28 last Saturday in Tokyo flew directly to the team’s camp in Lyon, France, soon after the match.

“He (Jake White) wants to see and have a feel of everyone in the current squad and assess them in the last three days before he makes a decision on naming the final squad for next weekend,” Sewabu said.

The Flying Fijians will begin their Nations Championship Test campaign against France in Lyon on Sunday, November 8 (Fiji time). They will then face Ireland in Dublin on Sunday, November 15 (Fiji time), before taking on Italy in Udine on Sunday, November 22.

At the team’s camp in Lyon, Europe-based players joined a three-day training camp.

The players included Pita Gus Sowakula, Josua Tuisova, Caleb Muntz, Salesi Rayasi, Pro D2 Player of the Year Seta Bituniyata, Jiuta Wainiqolo, Elia Canakaivata, Luke Tagi and Vinaya Habosi.

“We could only have them for three days and then they head back to their respective clubs for games this weekend. Then they will regroup back in Lyon after that, pending on injuries and then, obviously, with the squad announcement to be made on Friday by head coach Jake White and the management team. This also includes their assessment of the three-day camp that happened in Lyon in France,” Sewabu said.

The former Flying Fijians No. 8 said the main challenge as the team prepared for the Nations Championship was the limited time available for preparations.

“Our squad that is currently in Europe, the normal challenge and barrier for Fiji rugby is the ability to get them for enough preparation time. We’ve got the regulation time window for rugby, so we managed to get them for the next three days and for that, the message from the head coach is quite clear,” he said.

Sewabu confirmed that only about 10 players from the squad that faced Japan had travelled to Europe for the Nations Championship.

“There’s roughly around 10 players from the game against Japan that has gone up to Europe, plus the ones that have come through the European competition in France and England,” he added.

Meanwhile, emerging loose forward Motikiai Murray will miss the Nations Championship after receiving a four-match suspension from World Rugby. Murray was sent off against Japan for a dangerous tackle.

title: Stephen Gallacher rolls out 2027 Junior Ryder Cup qualification process
article_text:
Stephen Gallacher has thrown down the gauntlet to 2027 Junior Ryder Cup hopefuls as the Bathgate man bids to lead Europe to victory in the biennial event for a second time.

The qualification process for next year’s contest in Ireland - the opening two days are being held at Ballyneety Golf Club before the singles are played at Adare Manor - has been announced by Ryder Cup Europe and the European Golf Association.

Points will be up for grabs in ten tournaments, with the top three boys and top three girls securing automatic selection and the remaining six spots then being selected by Gallacher.

“Anyone under 18 on 1 January - boy or girl - can qualify next year,” said the European captain. “There will be a ten-tournament process and we will pick the best five scores out of the ten. So the more players play in, the better chance they have of living out their dreams and playing in a Junior Ryder Cup.”

The first qualifying events are the Portuguese Ladies’ Amateur and Portuguese Amateur Championships in January, with the last counting tournaments being the The R&A Boys and Girls’ Amateur Championships in August.

“I think the qualification process will help the kids as they are playing under a bit of pressure, which they are going to do at Ballyneety and Adare Manor,” added Gallacher.

The 2014 Ryder Cup player, who led Europe to victory in Rome in 2023 before seeing his side lose to the US in New York last year, will be paying particular attention to the Irish Boys’ and Girls’ Championships when they take place at Ballyneety in May.

“I will be watching those events very closely,” he admitted. “That will be a great warm up for me because whoever does well round there will certainly be in my thoughts for the Junior Ryder Cup. I think both courses are fantastic and the kids are so good now that they are ready for what lies ahead.”

The main hopes of a Scot making the team probably lies with Carly McDonald, the St Andrews teenager who won The R&A Under-16 Girls’ Championship this year. Blairgowrie’s Fraser Walters, who topped the Scottish Boys’ Order of Merit this season, will also have his sights set on making Gallacher’s line up.

Gallacher, who currently tops the Legends Tour Order of Merit, paid a visit to Ballyneety and Adare Manor earlier this month along with Paul McGinley, his captain in the aforementioned Ryder Cup at Gleneagles.
